metadata.name: [GCP Cloud SQL MySQL OTel] High CPU utilization
metadata.description: Alerts when the average CPU utilization of a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance over the last 15 minutes is at least 90% of its reserved vCPUs (the sample-weighted mean of database/cpu/utilization, with at least 5 samples). At this level, statements queue for CPU and query latency rises. Values above 100% are possible. The 15-minute average absorbs short spikes and allows for the 3-5 minute delivery delay.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.cloudsql_mysql.otel-*
| WHERE resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "cloudsql_database"
// Sample-weighted mean and peak of CPU utilization (fraction of reserved vCPUs, can exceed 1.0), plus the MySQL marker
| STATS cpu_total = SUM(SUM_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/cpu/utilization`)),
        cpu_samples = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/cpu/utilization`)),
        cpu_peak = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/cpu/utilization`)),
        marker = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/mysql/queries`))
  BY database_id

breach.segment:
// MySQL instances with at least 5 samples in the window
WHERE marker > 0 AND cpu_samples >= 5
| EVAL avg_cpu = cpu_total / cpu_samples
// Threshold: average at or above 90% of reserved CPU across the window
| WHERE avg_cpu >= 0.9
| EVAL avg_cpu_pct = ROUND(avg_cpu * 100, 1),
       peak_cpu_pct = ROUND(cpu_peak * 100, 1)
| SORT avg_cpu_pct DESC, database_id ASC
| LIMIT 100
| KEEP database_id, avg_cpu_pct, peak_cpu_pct, cpu_samples

data.content:
## Cloud SQL MySQL high CPU utilization

The instance has averaged at least 90% of its reserved vCPUs for about 15 minutes, so queries are competing for CPU.

### Triage
1. Open **[GCP OTel] Cloud SQL MySQL Instance Detail**. Compare *CPU utilization vs reserved cores* with *Queries per second*, *Slow query ratio*, *Threads connected, running and cached* and *InnoDB pages read and written per second*.
2. CPU rising with queries/s means a traffic increase. CPU rising with flat traffic but more page reads or slow queries means a query plan change or missing index, usually a full scan.
3. Threads running well above the reserved cores confirms CPU queueing.
4. Find the expensive statements with Query Insights in the Google Cloud console, or with `performance_schema` and `sys.statement_analysis`.

### Actions
Fix or kill the offending queries, add indexes, move read traffic to read replicas, or scale the instance to a larger tier.

### Tuning
Change `avg_cpu >= 0.9` to adjust the threshold, and the rule's time window to change how long the load must last.
